description: An Azure AI Foundry-focused application for classifying support tickets and demonstrating the value of model customization or fine-tuning. It is not a chatbot.

questions.question: Which language should the Classifier Web UI use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Recommended for a typed, maintainable web interface.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Use plain JavaScript for a lightweight web interface.

questions.rationale: A web UI is appropriate for entering tickets, inspecting classifications, and comparing baseline and customized model results.

questions.question: Which framework should the Classifier Web UI use?

options.label: React
options.description: Recommended for a component-based classifier and evaluation interface.

options.label: Angular
options.description: A structured framework for larger applications.

questions.rationale: React provides a straightforward path for the ticket-entry, results, and model-comparison views.

questions.question: What should the Classifier Web UI include?
questions.recommendedChoice: Ticket input, predicted category/priority, confidence, and a baseline-versus-customized model comparison view.
questions.answer: Ticket input, predicted category/priority, confidence, and a baseline-versus-customized model comparison view.
questions.rationale: These views keep the experience focused on ticket classification and make model-customization value observable without turning the product into a chatbot.

questions.question: Which language should the Classification API use?

options.label: Python
options.description: Recommended for model workflows, evaluation, and Azure AI Foundry integration.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: A typed option for an API-oriented backend.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Use a shared language across the web UI and API.

questions.rationale: Python has a mature ecosystem for model evaluation and customization workflows.

questions.question: Which framework should the Classification API use?

options.label: FastAPI
options.description: Recommended for a typed Python API with a concise development workflow.

questions.rationale: FastAPI fits a focused inference and evaluation API.

questions.question: What should the Classification API do?
questions.recommendedChoice: Validate ticket text, classify category and priority through an Azure AI Foundry model endpoint, and provide evaluation/comparison support for a baseline and customized model. Keep model training/deployment and Azure resource provisioning out of scope unless separately approved.
questions.answer: Validate ticket text, classify category and priority through an Azure AI Foundry model endpoint, and provide evaluation/comparison support for a baseline and customized model. Keep model training/deployment and Azure resource provisioning out of scope unless separately approved.
questions.rationale: This provides the requested Foundry-centered classification and fine-tuning demonstration while avoiding unapproved cloud provisioning.

questions.question: Which data stores are needed?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Choose only when the application does not need persistence, file/object storage, queues, cache, or service-associated storage.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Store ticket datasets and evaluation or customization files used in the model demonstration.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Persist ticket records, labels, or evaluation history in a relational database.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Persist ticket records, labels, or evaluation history in a relational database.

options.label: Cosmos DB
options.description: Persist ticket records or evaluation artifacts in a document database.

questions.rationale: Fine-tuning and evaluation demonstrations need dataset files; Blob Storage is recommended for those files. No ticket database is assumed.

questions.question: Should users sign in to use the application's API features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require user sign-in for application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: Keep application API features unauthenticated for the initial demonstration.

questions.rationale: The requested scope is a focused demonstration; identity-provider and Azure credential choices are intentionally not assumed.
